name: Haskell Type Safety & Purity
description: Enforces Haskell best practices for type safety, purity, and principled use of effects.
content:
# Haskell Type Safety & Purity Rules

- Add explicit type signatures to all top-level definitions — type inference is for local bindings, not your API
- Keep functions pure by default — only use `IO` when interacting with the outside world
- Use `newtype` for domain-specific wrappers — zero runtime cost, prevents mixing up arguments of the same base type
- Prefer `Text` over `String` for text data — `String` is a linked list of characters and performs poorly
- Use `Maybe` for optional values and `Either` for computations that can fail with an error message
- Enable `-Wall` and `-Werror` in CI — treat warnings as errors to catch partial functions and missing patterns
- Avoid partial functions (`head`, `tail`, `fromJust`, `read`) — use total alternatives or pattern match explicitly
- Use `do` notation for monadic sequencing — keep each line focused on one operation
- Prefer `Data.Map.Strict` and `Data.Set` over lists for lookups — lists are O(n) for membership checks
- Use `deriving` strategies (`stock`, `newtype`, `via`) to reduce boilerplate while staying explicit
- Handle errors with `ExceptT` or `MonadError` in your monad stack — don't throw exceptions in pure code
- Use `-XOverloadedStrings` and `-XDerivingStrategies` as project-wide default extensions
